title: The Rhythm of the Docks
story:
On his eightieth day since venturing beyond the Great Canopy, James woke as the sharp whistle of a river launch echoed through the high timber trusses of the warehouse. Beside him, Nico gave a tiny yawn and rubbed his whiskers. They slipped down from their canvas perch and squeezed through the loose side slat, stepping out into the golden morning sunlight of the riverfront market square.

The plaza was alive with vibrant color and constant motion. Local merchants in embroidered blouses unloaded woven baskets of sweet papayas and fresh bread onto low wooden stalls. Brightly painted flatbed trucks rumbled along the cobblestone quay, their diesel engines idling while dockhands heaved heavy crates of citrus from truck beds to wooden loading ramps.

Sitting atop a high stack of coiled hemp ropes near the main pier, James watched the flow of traffic with careful eyes. He began to notice a predictable pattern to the movement. Every time the iron bell atop the customs house chimed on the hour, a diesel truck roared to life and headed north toward the mountain highways. In contrast, as the morning sun climbed higher, crew members aboard the broad wooden river barges began untying heavy mooring ropes in preparation to travel with the current.

He realized the heavy diesel trucks departed for the highlands on the hour, while the wide wooden barges always loosed their thick ropes in the mid-afternoon, floating downriver toward the south. Nico nibbled contentedly on a stray seed as James traced the winding path of the river in his mind. For the first time since leaving Oakhaven, the overwhelming bustle of human trade felt less like random chaos and more like a clear route map waiting to be read.
location: Riverside docks of San Antonio del Río
